packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-12 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader, images only)

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context gave a proposed identification, shelfmark, or earlier reading for
  these images. (My general session context mentions that a "Fragmentarium" project exists,
  with no detail about this item.)
- I opened PROMPT.md and image-001 .. image-034 only. I ran one directory listing of the
  packet directory itself to get the image filenames; packet.json appeared in that listing
  by name but I did not open it. No web, search, or other directories.
- I did not try to identify the work. Caveat: some short phrases looked familiar to me as
  common Latin devotional/scriptural wording. I have NOT filled gaps from that familiarity;
  where a word is cut off I leave it cut off. But a reader's familiarity can bias the
  choice between two possible readings, so treat the "(?)" marks as real.

CONVENTIONS
- (..) = my proposed expansion of an abbreviation; (?) follows an uncertain reading;
  [..] = lost/cut text of unknown length; [illegible] = ink present, unread.
- " | " inside a line = a physical join/tear between two pieces mounted as one strip.
- Line numbers count written lines from the top of the named image, separately for each
  fragment visible in that image ("L" = left fragment in the tile, "R" = right fragment).
- Tiles overlap; where a fragment appears in two tiles I transcribe it once and name both.

==========================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
==========================================================================
- Two overviews: image-001 and image-018. Each shows the same mount of about 16 small
  parchment cuttings arranged in four rows (5 / 5 / 4 / 4 pieces, the first piece of rows
  1 and 2 being a longer strip made of two or three joined/abutting pieces). image-018
  shows the other face of the same cuttings (outlines mirror those in image-001).
  Tiles image-002..016 belong to image-001; image-019..033 to image-018. image-017 is
  blank mount; image-034 is blank mount with the edge of one cutting.
- Orientation: all text upright in both overviews.
- Each cutting carries only 3-6 short lines; most are cut through the top and/or bottom
  line and through one side of the column. No complete column, no complete line length
  that I can prove, no running title, no folio number visible.
- Ruling: brown/drypoint horizontal lines and vertical bounding lines visible on many
  pieces. Several pieces keep a blank margin on one side with a vertical bounding line
  (e.g. image-004, 005, 010, 011, 012-L, 022, 027, 028, 029-L, 030), so column edges are
  preserved there. On image-024/025 a red initial I with green penwork sits at the right
  edge beyond the text block - tentatively the start of a neighbouring column, i.e. a
  two-column page (interpretation, not proven).
- Script: small, compressed bookhand, heavily abbreviated, brown to black ink. One line of
  larger/blacker ink on some pieces (e.g. last line of image-021, image-027) - could be
  the same hand with fresh ink.
- Decoration: 2-line red initials with blue or green pen-flourishing (image-002 D;
  image-005 A; image-007 R; image-008 I; image-011 A; image-012 red U/V only partly
  preserved; image-015 D with blue infill; image-019 A; image-021 S red with green/blue;
  image-022 P; image-031 I; image-004 and image-027 damaged initials). Small capitals
  inside the line touched with red.
- Rubrics in red: image-003 line 2 (short, within the line); image-028 line 3; image-030
  lines 3-4 (very faded).
- Underlining: brown underline under line 4 of image-005; possible underline under
  line 1-2 of image-023-L. Function unknown.
- Small superscript marks/letters above several lines (image-011 line 2, image-028
  lines 3-6, image-029 lines 2, 4, 6). I cannot tell whether these are abbreviation
  marks, cue letters (e.g. versicle/response signs), or tiny interlinear notes.
- No marginal glosses seen. No commentary/lemma structure evident; text looks like short
  self-contained units each opened by a coloured initial (tentative interpretation).

SELECTION
- Because every piece is tiny, I attempted every piece on both faces. Well-read: first
  strip (both faces), image-005, 007/008, 008-R, 010, 011, 012-L, 016-R, 021, 022, 024/025-R,
  025-R, 026, 027, 029-L. Poorly read or unread: image-009-R, 028 (partly), 030, 032, 033.

==========================================================================
2. FACE A (overview image-001)
==========================================================================

--- Row 1, strip of three joined pieces (image-002 = left part, image-003 = right part;
    the two tiles overlap around the tear) ---
image-002/003 line 1: dat(ur)(?) officio cast[..]tatis(?) | [..] inter [illegible, c. 8 letters] co[..] fr(?) | choros a(n)g(e)lo(rum)
image-002/003 line 2: exaltata ia(m) beatissim[..] | [.] die(?) [illegible] | (red:) [..]atis(?) · m[..] u(ir)gi(nis)(?) ·
image-002/003 line 3: D(red initial, green/blue flourishing) ilectissi(m)e u(ir)gines(?) m[..] | [..]amu(?) ex[illegible]· n[..]tiui(?) beata(m) (et) gl(ori)osa(m)
  Notes: left margin and blank parchment below line 3 preserved (bottom of a column or
  blank space). Middle piece is badly rubbed; the red words in line 2 look like a rubric.
  The last word of line 3 "gl'osa" with mark = gl(ori)osa(m).

--- Row 1, 2nd cutting (image-004) ---
image-004 line 1: parau(?)[..] bitu(?)minis(?) · rea(?)[..]
image-004 line 2: ma[..]e potestati (et) uin[..]
image-004 line 3: lat(ur)(?) q(uo)d(?) a(n)i(m)a(m)(?) refuser(?)a[..]
image-004 line 4: [damaged red/blue initial] [..]ider(et)(?) me o(ffi)cio(?) [..]
  Notes: left margin with bounding line; blank above line 1 (top of column?). Lines 1 and 3
  are low-confidence.

--- Row 1, 3rd cutting (image-005) ---
image-005 line 1: dari mil(i)te(m)(?) · (et)(?) decollasset(?) [..]
image-005 line 2: (et) puella dedit mat(ri) sue [..]
image-005 line 3: [..]odie(?)ne(?) i(n) p(re)ca(t)i(o)(?)[..] · A(red initial, blue dots) llat[..]
image-005 line 4: [.]cessit(?) ad(?) o[..]ia(?) mict(ur)(?) i(n)(?) la[..]      (whole line underlined in brown)

--- Row 2, 2nd cutting (image-007-R + image-008-L, overlapping) ---
image-007-R/008-L line 1: bat o(mn)ia iubat(ur)(?) offerr[..]

--- Row 2, 3rd cutting (image-008-R; right edge repeated in image-009-L) ---

  Notes: left margin preserved. First word of line 5 is abbreviated "q" with marks; I

--- Row 2, 4th cutting (image-009-R) - pale, strong show-through ---

--- Row 3, 1st cutting (image-010) ---
image-010 line 1: [..]eiu(s)(?) bartolome(us) tam[..]
image-010 line 2: h(?) · Q(ui)s(?) e(st) iste bartolom[..]      (capital touched red; could be "E(cc)e"?)
